claims.text: This dispute rests on a single, internally consistent trip, so the rider's case is properly founded: EV-TRIP-00804, EV-GPS-00804 and EV-FARE-00804 all carry trip_id TRP-00804, and the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown agree on the 13:54 booking, the 13:59:30 arrival and the 4.88 km driven. The same-trip condition in POL-RD-08(a) is met and the burden of explanation passes to the driver under POL-RD-08.

The trace the rider's case rests on is clean and carries its full weight: EV-GPS-00804 holds 79 fixes over 100% coverage on a 10-second sample interval, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 10 seconds, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and nothing in this case turns on an impaired artifact; the case can be decided on the trace itself without any escalation under POL-RD-10(3), and the artifact stands at weight 1.0 under POL-GEN-02.

On the POL-RD-01 threshold test the governing measurement is the GPS polyline, not the rounded convenience copy: EV-GPS-00804 records trace_distance_km of 4.88 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, and that is the figure the excess must be run on.

I have to concede the threshold is not met, and I will not stretch the point. Measured against the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km, the trace shows an excess of 0.13 km, which is 2.74% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and neither test passes, so no route deviation is established on this trip and the rider's refund claim fails on the evidence as measured.

The claim as filed also measures the trip against the wrong baseline, and I concede that ground too: the rider's 3.10 km figure is solo_optimal_distance_km, but TRP-00804 is a RYDE_POOL trip and under POL-RD-12 the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km, with the solo estimate carried for reference only. Distance attributable to collecting the co-rider at Queenstown is never a deviation, so no part of it is refundable to the rider.

For completeness on the driver's side of the ledger: no traffic advisory covers this trip at all. EV-ADVIS-00804-01 is MISSING, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, so under POL-GEN-02 it can carry no fact. I disclose that impairment expressly. If any external traffic cause is later advanced, POL-RD-13 gives such an assertion no weight where no advisory covers the trip window and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record — though I note no such cause is in fact asserted on the present record.

claims.text: The rider's claim is measured against the wrong baseline. This trip is RYDE_POOL, so under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km recorded on the trip record at booking, and not the solo-rider estimate of 3.10 km the rider cites. POL-RD-12 states in terms that a claim which measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The record is complete on this point and no POL-RD-10(5) gap arises: the trip record identifies the pooled itinerary through vehicle_type RYDE_POOL and optimal_route_source PLATFORM_MATCHED_ITINERARY_AT_BOOKING, and carries the matched itinerary as optimal_distance_km.

On the correct pooled baseline the trace shows no deviation at all. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 4.88 km, against the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km — an excess of 0.13 km, or 2.74%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal and 0.8 km in absolute terms; this excess fails both limbs by a wide margin, and the policy's own derived deviation block records the status as 'no deviation'. Where the trace figure and the trip record's rounded copy agree, as they do here, nothing turns on the choice, but the trace is the field that governs.

The very thing the rider complains of — the collection of another passenger at Queenstown — is excluded from excess by POL-RD-12. The trip record's own event log confirms the matched pooled itinerary at 13:55 and states that the co-rider pickup at Queenstown is included in the 4.75 km estimate. Distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation. The rider's central factual allegation, even if true, is therefore not a route deviation in law.

Even if a deviation were established, POL-RD-02 would refund nothing. Recomputed on the booked optimal route — (3.80 + 0.75 x 4.75 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee — the fare is 12.0825 SGD, which EXCEEDS the 11.90 SGD actually charged. Refund = charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero, so the refund is 0.00, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and the outcome is NO_ACTION in any event. The ledger's own derived money block computes refund_before_rounding of 0 and marks the refund below de minimis.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The trace is COMPLETE and is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 79 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 10 seconds. There is therefore no impaired-trace route to an independent corroborating source under POL-RD-07(ii), and the ordinary POL-RD-01 threshold test applied to that clean trace fails. An assertion of excess that cites no evidence id of its own carries no weight.

No billing-integrity correction is available to the rider under POL-RD-09(4). The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and no tolls (both 0.00) and no airport surcharge; the 0.80 SGD platform fee is a standard structured line of the fare model. There is no charge line that the trace or the trip record fails to match, so the one route to a refund that is available whether or not a deviation exists is closed.

Even if the materiality gate had been reached, POL-RD-06 discloses no pattern against this driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 300 completed trips in the same window — below the 3-flag trigger and a ratio of 0.00, far under the 0.05 threshold. There is no basis for the balance to be resolved against the driver, for a FULL_REFUND uplift, or for a conduct referral, and no other profile field is used for that test.

Every artifact the driver relies on carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired, so no disclosure obligation arises and no discount attaches to the finding under POL-GEN-02. The only impaired artifact in the bundle is the traffic advisory, which the driver does not rely on and does not need, because no deviation was established that would require exoneration.

NO_ACTION is the correct outcome and on this record it is a win for the driver. The rider filed this dispute, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so leaving the present state standing preserves the fare the driver earned on a completed pooled trip. The driver asks that the claim be dismissed; he does not ask for the fare to be varied, and no compensation is sought because the billed distance of 4.88 km equals the trace distance, leaving no unbilled shortfall above 1.0 km.

ruling.explanation: The fare you were charged stands, and the refund you asked for is not due. The reason is the baseline the claim uses. Trip TRP-00804 is a RYDE_POOL trip, so under POL-RD-12 the figure the route-deviation test runs against is the platform-matched pooled itinerary of 4.75 km stored on EV-TRIP-00804, not the solo-rider estimate of 3.10 km in your claim. The solo figure is carried on the record for reference only, and the clause says a claim measured against it cites the wrong field; the driver's and your own advocate's briefs both correct this. Measured the right way, EV-GPS-00804 records a trace of 4.88 km over a clean export (79 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps), giving an excess of 0.13 km, or 2.74% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and neither limb is met, so no route deviation is established on this trip. The distance used to collect the co-rider at Queenstown is separately excluded from excess by POL-RD-12, so the collection itself is not a deviation in law however inconvenient it was. The arithmetic confirms the point from the other direction: on EV-FARE-00804 the charged_total is SGD 11.90 and the recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 4.75 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 12.0825, so the refund under POL-RD-02 is charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero — SGD 0.00, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis. No billing-integrity correction is available under POL-RD-09(4): the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and the SGD 0.80 platform fee is a standard line of the fare model, so there is no unmatched charge to refund. There is no repeat-deviation pattern under POL-RD-06 — the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 300 completed trips in the same window, well under both triggers — so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral arises. The only impaired artifact in the bundle is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00804-01 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0); it can carry no fact, and because nobody asserts an external traffic cause for this trip, its absence decides nothing and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. No driver compensation is due either: the billed distance of 4.88 km equals the trace distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall. The route-deviation claim is therefore dismissed on the evidence: under POL-GEN-03 the present state stands, the charge remains in place and nothing is refunded. Confidence is 0.95, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-GPS-00804, EV-TRIP-00804, EV-FARE-00804) that carry the deciding measurements; the monetary effect is nil, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold. This ruling is provisional, and either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

This is a RYDE_POOL trip, and that decides the case. Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for the route-deviation test is the matched-itinerary optimal recorded at booking on EV-TRIP-00804, which is 4.75 km — not the solo-rider estimate of 3.10 km the rider filed against. The trip record identifies the pooled itinerary (vehicle_type RYDE_POOL, optimal_route_source PLATFORM_MATCHED_ITINERARY_AT_BOOKING) and its own event log states at 13:55 that the co-rider pickup at Queenstown is included in the 4.75 km estimate. Distance spent collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation, so the very thing complained of is excluded by POL-RD-12, and a claim measured against the 3.10 km solo figure has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. On the correct baseline the measured excess is: the governing figure is the GPS polyline on EV-GPS-00804, trace_distance_km = 4.88 km (not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record), against the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km — an excess of 0.13 km, or 2.74%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km in absolute terms; 0.13 km fails both limbs by a wide margin. No route deviation is established, and the outcome is NO_ACTION. Two further checks confirm no money moves even on the contrary assumption: on POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is (3.80 + 0.75 x 4.75 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 12.0825 SGD, which exceeds charged_total of 11.90 SGD, so the refund (charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero) is 0.00 and below the 0.50 SGD de minimis (EV-FARE-00804); and there is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), because the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry line, no toll and no airport surcharge — every charge line is matched. No driver compensation arises under POL-RD-04: the billed distance of 4.88 km equals the trace distance of 4.88 km, leaving no unbilled shortfall above 1.0 km. The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not triggered, because no MATERIAL deviation exists; for completeness the citable fields show driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 300 completed trips in the window, so no pattern is disclosed and no conduct referral follows. On the missing artifact: EV-ADVIS-00804-01 (a traffic advisory) is MISSING, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so under POL-GEN-02 it can carry no fact — but no party advances an external traffic cause, so nothing is invoked against it and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged; its absence is recorded only. The GPS trace is clean and not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) (79 fixes, 100% coverage, 10-second sampling, max gap 10 seconds), and every artifact the finding rests on carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, so confidence is not discounted and no escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands: payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00 on EV-FARE-00804. The monetary effect is 0.00, below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes on issue; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

To both parties — this ruling concerns trip TRP-00804 (Buona Vista MRT to Tiong Bahru MRT, 14 Aug 2026), a pooled RYDE_POOL trip for which the rider was charged SGD 11.90. Payment status remains CHARGED and no money moves.

Why the refund is refused. The rider's case is that the trip should have been 3.10 km and that the driver detoured to Queenstown to collect another passenger. The 3.10 km figure is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km. This is a pooled trip: vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL and optimal_route_source is PLATFORM_MATCHED_ITINERARY_AT_BOOKING. Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for a pooled trip is the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km recorded at booking, not the solo estimate, and distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation. The claim as filed measures against the wrong field and fails on that ground (POL-RD-12).

On the correct baseline, the governing measurement is the GPS polyline. EV-GPS-00804 records trace_distance_km of 4.88 km, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure, not the trip record's rounded copy, the field for the threshold test. The excess over 4.75 km is 0.13 km, or 2.74% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km in absolute terms; neither test passes, so no deviation is established and no POL-RD-02 refund arises. Even had one been established, the recomputation is (3.80 + 0.75 x 4.75 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge (read from EV-FARE-00804) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 12.0825, which EXCEEDS the SGD 11.90 charged; refund = 11.90 less 12.0825, floored at zero, is SGD 0.00, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, giving NO_ACTION in any event.

Other routes to payment were checked and none applies. POL-RD-09(4): the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00804) carries no ERP lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and every line matches the trace and trip record, so there is no billing-integrity correction; the SGD 0.80 platform fee is a standard structured line. POL-RD-06: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 300 completed trips in the same window, below the 3-flag trigger and a ratio of 0.00 against the 0.05 threshold, so no pattern is established, the balance is not shifted and no conduct referral arises.

Trace integrity and weight. EV-GPS-00804 is clean — 79 fixes, 100% coverage, a 10-second sample interval, no gaps and a 10-second maximum gap — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises, and it stands at weight 1.0 (POL-GEN-02). The only artifact below weight 1.0 is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00804-01, which is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0; it can carry no fact, but no party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is not invoked and its absence decides nothing (POL-RD-13). The deciding facts — the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km and the trace distance of 4.88 km — are carried by EV-TRIP-00804 and EV-GPS-00804, both at weight 1.0, so confidence is capped at 1.0 and stands at 0.95, above the 0.70 floor.

On the advocates' claims: the rider's own submissions concede the threshold is not met (claim 4) and that the solo baseline is the wrong field (claim 5), which the driver's claims 1 to 3 assert on the same points; they are answered together above and accepted. The driver's claims on POL-RD-02 (claim 4), POL-RD-09 (claim 6), POL-RD-06 (claim 7), POL-GEN-02 (claim 8) and POL-GEN-03 (claim 9) are accepted. The rider's claims on same-trip identity (claim 1) and trace integrity (claim 2) are accepted, as is the rider's disclosure of the MISSING advisory (claim 6). No claim was discarded by the referee and none is discarded by me.

Effect and next steps. The monetary effect is SGD nil, below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so nothing needs to be held or released. This ruling is provisional; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. No referral is issued, because the clauses that produce referrals — POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review and POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity — did not fire on this record.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute asks whether the SGD 11.90 fare on trip TRP-00804 should be refunded as a route deviation. It should not, and the charge stands.

Baseline (POL-RD-12). The trip was RYDE_POOL. Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for measuring any deviation is the matched-itinerary optimal distance of 4.75 km recorded at booking on EV-TRIP-00804 (optimal_route_source PLATFORM_MATCHED_ITINERARY_AT_BOOKING), not the solo-rider estimate of 3.10 km the rider cites. The platform's own event log records that the co-rider pickup at Queenstown is included in the 4.75 km figure, and distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation. A claim measured against solo_optimal_distance_km (3.10 km) has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone.

Threshold (POL-RD-01). The governing measurement is the GPS polyline, and EV-GPS-00804 records trace_distance_km of 4.88 km. Against the 4.75 km matched-itinerary optimal that is an excess of 0.13 km, or 2.74%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH more than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND more than 0.8 km absolute; neither test passes, so no route deviation is established. The rider's advocate conceded this expressly, and the driver's advocate reaches the same figure.

Fare arithmetic (POL-RD-02), had a deviation existed. Recomputed on the booked optimal route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 4.75 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge, read from EV-FARE-00804, + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 12.0825. That exceeds the SGD 11.90 actually charged. Refund = charged_total (11.90) less recomputed_fare (12.0825), floored at zero = SGD 0.00, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis. So the refund line is nil on either route to the decision.

Pass-through lines (POL-RD-09(4)). EV-FARE-00804 carries no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge; there is no charge line the trace or trip record fails to match. The one refund route that is available whether or not a deviation exists is therefore closed.

The rider's advisory point. EV-ADVIS-00804-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; the rider correctly disclosed that. Nothing turns on it: no external traffic cause is asserted by anyone, no POL-RD-03 exoneration is invoked, and POL-RD-13 therefore has no work to do. Its absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5), because no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact.

Trace integrity and escalation. EV-GPS-00804 is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 79 fixes, 100% coverage, 10-second interval, no gaps, maximum gap 10 seconds. POL-RD-07 and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route are not engaged, and the rule in POL-RD-10(1) is met because confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. Trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00804, EV-GPS-00804 and EV-FARE-00804; timestamps do not conflict; the computed refund does not exceed SGD 150.00 or charged_total; and no charge line lacks a counterpart. No escalation trigger fires.

Driver profile (POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01). driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 300 completed trips in the same window — no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift, no driver-conduct referral. No profile field outside those POL-GEN-01 names as a ground was used by either side, and the referee discarded no claim.

Outcome (POL-GEN-03). NO_ACTION: the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands — the SGD 11.90 charge on EV-FARE-00804 is left in place, with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00. No driver compensation is owed: the billed distance of 4.88 km equals the trace distance, leaving no unbilled shortfall above 1.0 km. No clause produces a referral. The monetary effect is SGD 0.00, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold under POL-GEN-05, so nothing is held or executed. This is a provisional ruling and either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: This dispute rests on a single, internally consistent trip, so the rider's case is properly founded: EV-TRIP-00804, EV-GPS-00804 and EV-FARE-00804 all carry trip_id TRP-00804, and the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown agree on the 13:54 booking, the 13:59:30 arrival and the 4.88 km driven. The same-trip condition in POL-RD-08(a) is met and the burden of explanation passes to the driver under POL-RD-08.

The trace the rider's case rests on is clean and carries its full weight: EV-GPS-00804 holds 79 fixes over 100% coverage on a 10-second sample interval, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 10 seconds, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and nothing in this case turns on an impaired artifact; the case can be decided on the trace itself without any escalation under POL-RD-10(3), and the artifact stands at weight 1.0 under POL-GEN-02.

On the POL-RD-01 threshold test the governing measurement is the GPS polyline, not the rounded convenience copy: EV-GPS-00804 records trace_distance_km of 4.88 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, and that is the figure the excess must be run on.

I have to concede the threshold is not met, and I will not stretch the point. Measured against the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km, the trace shows an excess of 0.13 km, which is 2.74% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and neither test passes, so no route deviation is established on this trip and the rider's refund claim fails on the evidence as measured.

The claim as filed also measures the trip against the wrong baseline, and I concede that ground too: the rider's 3.10 km figure is solo_optimal_distance_km, but TRP-00804 is a RYDE_POOL trip and under POL-RD-12 the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km, with the solo estimate carried for reference only. Distance attributable to collecting the co-rider at Queenstown is never a deviation, so no part of it is refundable to the rider.

For completeness on the driver's side of the ledger: no traffic advisory covers this trip at all. EV-ADVIS-00804-01 is MISSING, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, so under POL-GEN-02 it can carry no fact. I disclose that impairment expressly. If any external traffic cause is later advanced, POL-RD-13 gives such an assertion no weight where no advisory covers the trip window and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record — though I note no such cause is in fact asserted on the present record.

The rider's claim is measured against the wrong baseline. This trip is RYDE_POOL, so under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km recorded on the trip record at booking, and not the solo-rider estimate of 3.10 km the rider cites. POL-RD-12 states in terms that a claim which measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The record is complete on this point and no POL-RD-10(5) gap arises: the trip record identifies the pooled itinerary through vehicle_type RYDE_POOL and optimal_route_source PLATFORM_MATCHED_ITINERARY_AT_BOOKING, and carries the matched itinerary as optimal_distance_km.

On the correct pooled baseline the trace shows no deviation at all. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 4.88 km, against the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km — an excess of 0.13 km, or 2.74%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal and 0.8 km in absolute terms; this excess fails both limbs by a wide margin, and the policy's own derived deviation block records the status as 'no deviation'. Where the trace figure and the trip record's rounded copy agree, as they do here, nothing turns on the choice, but the trace is the field that governs.

The very thing the rider complains of — the collection of another passenger at Queenstown — is excluded from excess by POL-RD-12. The trip record's own event log confirms the matched pooled itinerary at 13:55 and states that the co-rider pickup at Queenstown is included in the 4.75 km estimate. Distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation. The rider's central factual allegation, even if true, is therefore not a route deviation in law.

Even if a deviation were established, POL-RD-02 would refund nothing. Recomputed on the booked optimal route — (3.80 + 0.75 x 4.75 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee — the fare is 12.0825 SGD, which EXCEEDS the 11.90 SGD actually charged. Refund = charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero, so the refund is 0.00, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and the outcome is NO_ACTION in any event. The ledger's own derived money block computes refund_before_rounding of 0 and marks the refund below de minimis.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The trace is COMPLETE and is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 79 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 10 seconds. There is therefore no impaired-trace route to an independent corroborating source under POL-RD-07(ii), and the ordinary POL-RD-01 threshold test applied to that clean trace fails. An assertion of excess that cites no evidence id of its own carries no weight.

No billing-integrity correction is available to the rider under POL-RD-09(4). The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and no tolls (both 0.00) and no airport surcharge; the 0.80 SGD platform fee is a standard structured line of the fare model. There is no charge line that the trace or the trip record fails to match, so the one route to a refund that is available whether or not a deviation exists is closed.

Even if the materiality gate had been reached, POL-RD-06 discloses no pattern against this driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 300 completed trips in the same window — below the 3-flag trigger and a ratio of 0.00, far under the 0.05 threshold. There is no basis for the balance to be resolved against the driver, for a FULL_REFUND uplift, or for a conduct referral, and no other profile field is used for that test.

Every artifact the driver relies on carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired, so no disclosure obligation arises and no discount attaches to the finding under POL-GEN-02. The only impaired artifact in the bundle is the traffic advisory, which the driver does not rely on and does not need, because no deviation was established that would require exoneration.

NO_ACTION is the correct outcome and on this record it is a win for the driver. The rider filed this dispute, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so leaving the present state standing preserves the fare the driver earned on a completed pooled trip. The driver asks that the claim be dismissed; he does not ask for the fare to be varied, and no compensation is sought because the billed distance of 4.88 km equals the trace distance, leaving no unbilled shortfall above 1.0 km.
